title: Existence of a balanced orientation
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph. Then $G$ admits an orientation $D$ in which the in- and outdegrees at every vertex differ by at most one; that is, $\abs{d^{+}(v) - d^{-}(v)} \le 1$ for every vertex $v$, where $d^{+}(v)$ and $d^{-}(v)$ denote the outdegree and indegree of $v$ in $D$.
hypotheses_covered: G is a finite simple graph
replaced:
\emph{Show that \texttt{G} has an orientation
\texttt{D} such that \texttt{|d$^{+}$(v) - d$^{-}$(v)| $\le$ 1} for all \texttt{v $\in$ V}.}
